_readme: Small knowledge base for the Energy & Comfort Companion. Each entry quotes or closely paraphrases an official source (STEG) or an ANME statement as reported by the press, with its URL. Keywords include French, Arabic and Tunisian Darija (Arabic and Latin script) so simple keyword retrieval works across languages. Add entries only with a source.

docs.title: STEG residential electricity prices (low voltage, from 1 May 2022, excluding taxes)
docs.text: Residential prices in millimes per kWh depend on the monthly consumption: 62 if it does not exceed 50 kWh/month, 96 between 51 and 100 kWh/month (économique tranche: 1 and 2 kVA), 176 between 101 and 200, 218 between 201 and 300, 341 between 301 and 500, 414 above 500 kWh/month. In the official table each price applies to the whole monthly consumption in that band. Power fee (redevance de puissance): 700 millimes per kVA per month.

docs.title: Taxes on a residential STEG electricity bill
docs.text: VAT: 7% for domestic customers consuming 300 kWh/month or less, otherwise 13%, on the energy price excluding taxes. Plus a municipal surtax of 5 millimes/kWh and the Energy Transition Fund (FTE) tax of 5 millimes/kWh, except for low-voltage économique customers whose consumption does not exceed 100 kWh/month. (The tariff PDF of May 2022 listed FTE at 1 millime/kWh and VAT at 13%; the current web page gives the values above.)

docs.title: Bill based on a meter reading (facture sur relève)
docs.text: This bill is calculated from the customer's real consumption, deduced from the reading of the meter indexes. The bill on reading is bimonthly, following a reading every four months in towns or every six months in rural areas.

docs.title: Estimated bill
docs.text: The bill can be estimated if the meter indexes could not be read by STEG; in that case it is calculated from an estimate based on the consumption of the last 24 months.

docs.title: Intermediate bill (facture intermédiaire)
docs.text: This bill contains the estimated amount of your consumption calculated from your previous consumption, plus the fixed charges due, the estimated amount of the RTT contribution and various payment facilities (connection or other). The net amount of this bill is an advance: it is deducted from the bill that contains the real readings of your consumption. No advance is billed to new subscribers until they are read.

docs.title: ANME: set the air conditioner to 26 °C
docs.text: The ANME (national agency for energy management) asks households to set air conditioners to 26 °C, as a compromise between thermal comfort, energy efficiency and health. According to the agency, each degree below 26 °C increases electricity consumption by about 7%, and setting 18 °C does not cool a room faster.
docs.source: ANME campaign, reported by La Presse (6 July 2026) and AllAfrica (13 July 2026)

docs.title: ANME: shift consumption out of the summer peak
docs.text: The ANME asks citizens to adapt their consumption, in particular during the summer peak period from 11:00 to 16:00, and stresses regular maintenance of electrical equipment.

docs.title: INBETWEEN passive shading (what is and is not known)
docs.text: INBETWEEN screens are designed with a solar model (pvlib clear-sky irradiance on the facade and a perforated-screen transmission model). They estimate how much solar heat is blocked at the window on a hot clear day. Electricity savings have not yet been measured or validated: blocked solar heat is not the same as saved kWh on the bill, because it depends on the room, insulation, the air conditioner and how it is used.
docs.source: INBETWEEN design engine (model estimate, not measured)
